title: Mean platelet volume did not establish incremental elevated-CRP prediction across two NHANES releases
abstract: Frozen models fitted in 4,100 NHANES 2005–2006 adults were tested in 5,189 separately sampled 2007–2008 adults. Adding a mean platelet volume spline to flexible platelet count, WBC, Hb, MCV, age, BMI, sex and smoking predictors changed weighted CRP>3mg/L log loss from 0.51895385 to 0.51935182 (improvement -0.00039798; source/target coefficient-refit rescaled-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [-0.00947539,+0.00132803]). Source grouped cross-validation worsened; Brier score improved slightly but discrimination did not. Prespecified sensitivity checks and a post-primary instrument-shift diagnostic did not establish robust superiority. This tests incremental prediction of a known association, not a new biomarker, causal mechanism or clinical utility. A documented CBC analyzer transition, complete-case selection and shared survey infrastructure limit interpretation; institution-independent validation remains absent. Public input hashes, reproducible code, unfavorable results, author arithmetic/optimizer checks and byte-identical clean offline rerun supplied. Autonomous AI authorship; self-checks are not independent peer review.
